definition: A diagram that draws the sample space as a rectangle and each event as a circle inside it; where circles overlap, the outcomes are in both events.
The event $A \cap B$, read "$A$ and $B$": the outcomes that are in both events.
The event $A \cup B$, read "$A$ or $B$": the outcomes in at least one of the events, including those in both.
Events that cannot both happen, so $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = 0$.
The probability $\mathrm{P}(A \mid B)$ that $A$ happens given that $B$ has happened, found as $\frac{\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}$.
A diagram with one set of labelled branches for each stage of an experiment; you multiply probabilities along a path and add across paths.
Choosing items one after another without putting each one back, so the total, and the probabilities, change after every pick.
Events where one happening does not change the probability of the other, so $\mathrm{P}(A \cap B) = \mathrm{P}(A)\,\mathrm{P}(B)$.
